shots.prompt:

Input image 2 (scene-03.png) is reference ONLY for the same red tractor identity and the yellow logging crane's front-of-trailer mounting relationship. Do not copy its empty cargo state, forward camera, foreground characters or landscape.

Correct the machinery connection in input 1. We are looking from behind the log trailer toward the back of the tractor; the tractor faces AWAY toward the left distance. Place ONE clearly legible yellow rotating crane pedestal bolted to the FRONT structural frame of the LOG TRAILER, directly BEHIND the tractor cab and AHEAD of the cargo headboard and first cargo stakes. Make a visible continuous mechanical path from the bolted pedestal through the yellow articulated boom, its joints, black hydraulic cylinders and hoses to the EXISTING dark grapple holding the SAME third round oak log above the two loaded logs. Let the base and its lower boom connection be readable beside the rear of the cab rather than disappearing behind its roof. The cab roof stays intact, visibly independent and free of any crane mounting. The crane is part of the trailer; the tractor pulls this separate trailer through a drawbar/hitch, visible where the view allows. Do not fuse the trailer frame into the tractor.

Keep the SAME rear three-quarter camera, tractor facing away-left, trailer closest to viewer, same trailer chassis length, EXACTLY TWO trailer axles (the same two near-side trailer wheels), same large rear/small front tractor wheels and red tractor rims. Preserve the two loaded round bark-covered oak logs, the same suspended third log, load heights, stake locations and red-tipped dark steel stakes, rear lights, forest track, uprooted tree at left, stacked timber at left, stream at right, morning light, textures and warm dimensional storybook style. Keep background, framing and exposure as close to image 1 as possible.

Keep the SAME beaver driver in blue denim vest and tiny Mr. PinPin hedgehog inside their separate cab seats, same faces, expressions, relative scale and clothing. This is the BACK window of the cab: occupants look back toward the loading operation; the driver may turn toward crane control levers. No front-facing steering wheel positioned at the rear window, no duplicated faces or limbs, no new characters. Preserve all unrelated parts. No text, labels, borders, panels or watermarks. Render one full-bleed corrected candidate, not a before/after montage.
